record.paper_title: Five open problems in theory of quantum information
record.context_brief: Quantum orthogonal Latin squares of order six
record.original_question: Determine whether two quantum orthogonal Latin squares of order 6 exist. Equivalently, decide whether the classical 36 officers obstruction can be overcome by replacing the officers or cards with quantum states in H_6⊗H_6 arranged as a 6×6 table of 36 mutually orthogonal normalized vectors whose row and column superpositions are maximally entangled; a negative decision is equivalent to proving that there is no absolutely maximally entangled state of four six-level subsystems, no ((4,1,3))_6 quantum error-correction code, no 2-unitary matrix in U(36), and no perfect tensor with four indices each running from 1 to 6.

evidence.quote: Problem 3: Determine whether there exist two quantum orthogonal Latin squares [77, 78] of order six. In other words, find a solution of the problem of 36 ‘entangled officers’ of Euler or demonstrate that it does not exist.

Orthogonal quantum Latin squares(OQLS) are defined [77] as a collection of N2 normalized vectors from a composite spaceHN⊗HN, which are mutually orthogonal so they form an orthonormal basis. They are arranged in anN×N table such that for every row (column) the symmetric superposition of all states in each row (column) is a maximally entangled state.

As there are no two orthogonal Latin squares (OLS) of order six, the famous classical problem of36 officers of Euler has no solution [100]. An analogous quantum problem, which involves 36 entangled officers, remains open.

Establishing a negative result concerning existence of two quantum orthogonal Latin squares of order six is equivalent to proving that i) there is no AME state of four subsystems with six levels each [97, 103] thus the corresponding quantum error correction code [104], written((4, 1, 3))6, does not exist; ii) there is no 2-unitary matrixU ∈ U(36); iii) there is no perfect tensor with four indices, each running from 1 to 6.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem was solved affirmatively by Rather, Burchardt, Bruzda, Rajchel-Mieldzioć, Lakshminarayan, and Życzkowski (arXiv:2104.05122; Phys. Rev. Lett. 128, 080507, published February 2022). They explicitly constructed a pair of quantum orthogonal Latin squares of order 6, equivalently an AME(4,6) state (the "golden" AME state involving the golden ratio), a 2-unitary in U(36), a perfect 4-index tensor of dimension 6, and a $((4,1,3))_6$ code.

status_evidence.title: Thirty-six entangled officers of Euler: Quantum solution to a classically impossible problem
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum solution to the problem of 36 officers of Euler; construction of two orthogonal quantum Latin squares of order six and AME(4,6).
status_evidence.claim: The quantum analogue of Euler's 36 officers problem is solved positively: two quantum orthogonal Latin squares of order 6 exist.

status_evidence.title: Phys. Rev. Lett. 128, 080507 (2022)
status_evidence.snippet: Published 25 February 2022 — explicit construction of an AME state of four subsystems with six levels each.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of AME(4,6), equivalent to the existence of two quantum orthogonal Latin squares of order 6, is established.

status_evidence.title: Euler's 243-Year-Old 'Impossible' Puzzle Gets a Quantum Solution

status_evidence.claim: Independent science journalism confirms the resolution of the quantum 36-officers problem.
